scope: Selected expandable corpus; no exhaustive-book claim, physical replication or generic free-energy/antigravity discovery.

sources.title: De motu corporum in gyrum
sources.sections: Theorem 2, corollary 5 and Theorem 3; normalized Latin transcription.
sources.readDepth: Selected primary passage; not complete manuscript or facsimile collation.
sources.claim: Circular period/radius relations constrain a centripetal-force scaling.
sources.limits: The familiar modern circular reconstruction needs its kinematic assumptions; this passage does not alone establish a many-body law.
sources.provenance: Newton manuscript, Newton Project scholarly transcription.

sources.title: New Theory about Light and Colors
sources.sections: Printed pp. 3076–3078: prism, aperture/thickness/incidence controls and second-prism experiment.
sources.readDepth: Selected primary letter in normalized transcription.
sources.claim: Newton varied competing explanations for an elongated spectrum and used a second prism to compare selected rays.
sources.limits: Modern stipulated-index Snell diagrams are reconstructions, not measured historical spectra or a complete microscopic theory.
sources.provenance: Philosophical Transactions 80; Newton Project transcription.

sources.title: Opticks Book III, Query 31
sources.sections: Closing analysis/synthesis discussion, printed pp. 380–382.
sources.readDepth: Selected primary published passage.
sources.claim: Analysis from observations and synthesis of consequences are presented as revisable methods.
sources.limits: Historical authority does not prove a modern hypothesis; queries are questions, not all experimentally established laws.
sources.provenance: Newton published text, Newton Project transcription.

sources.title: Experiments, Portsmouth Add. MS 3973
sources.sections: Opening December 1678 entries ff. 1r–1v: weights, residues, appearance and failed mixtures.
sources.readDepth: Selected primary notebook transcription; no chemical experiment repeated.
sources.claim: Entries preserve measured quantities and unsuccessful combinations within early-modern chymistry.
sources.limits: Appearance and historical names do not identify modern composition or prove transmutation; no hazardous recipe is adopted.
sources.provenance: The Chymistry of Isaac Newton scholarly edition.

sources.title: Keynes MS 28: Emerald Tablet translation
sources.sections: Catalogue and English translation ff. 2r–2v; Latin commentary not translated.
sources.readDepth: Selected primary transcription plus editorial metadata.
sources.claim: Newton copied/translated an existing Hermetic text employing correspondence and separation imagery.
sources.limits: This is not a new Newtonian physical law, a proof of scale equivalence or evidence of every occult practice attributed to him.
sources.provenance: Newton manuscript of an older attributed text; Chymistry edition.

sources.title: Yahuda 7.3g/7.3o: Newton’s 2060 chronological notes
sources.sections: Yahuda 7.3g f. 13v normalized text; 7.3o f. 8r diplomatic text; Snobelen’s dating discussion.
sources.readDepth: Selected primary scholarly transcriptions directly read; manuscript images not collated.
sources.claim: Theological day/year interpretation and selected historical starting dates lead to qualified chronological bounds.
sources.limits: Not a mechanics prediction or verified apocalypse date. The diplomatic 7.3o line leaves its upper bound blank; do not silently fill it from a later explanation. Exact dating remains source-specific.
sources.provenance: Newton Project primary-text editions; historian commentary used separately.

sources.title: Alchemical Glossary: The Chymistry of Isaac Newton
sources.sections: Selected entries: Luna, Mars, Mercury, Regulus, Saturn, Sol, Sulfur, Venus, Niter, Sal ammoniac, Salt of tartar, Stibium, Vermilion, Vitriol.
sources.readDepth: Selected editorial reference entries; read earlier in this session.
sources.claim: Planetary and chymical names have contextual literal and disguised uses.
sources.limits: Candidate formulas remain hypotheses about a term; no historical specimen was assayed.
sources.provenance: Chymistry project scholarly glossary.

sources.title: Experiments with Alternate Currents of High Potential and High Frequency
sources.sections: Fig. 2 source/condenser/induction-coil chain; Fig. 3 coil, terminal capacity and enclosing metal screen discussion; selected introductory experiments.
sources.readDepth: Selected primary lecture transcription; not entire book.
sources.claim: The lecture specifies external excitation and notes that the surrounding metal changes capacitive/electromagnetic response and losses.
sources.limits: Spectacular discharge and voltage amplification do not establish excess energy. Historical high-voltage/body-contact demonstrations are not the modern protocol.
sources.provenance: Tesla lecture; Gutenberg ebook 13476, updated 2024-10-28; matching selected PBS transcript inspected.

sources.title: US685957A Apparatus for the utilization of radiant energy

sources.limits: Does not establish: a source-free energy demonstration or validated historical microscopic radiation model. Performance and conversion efficiency were not independently tested in this review.

sources.title: In-depth experimental search for a coupling between gravity and electromagnetism with steady fields
sources.sections: Selected author PDF §§2.1–2.3, §3 results, §4 conclusion; journal metadata only.
sources.readDepth: Selected full text read earlier in this session; carried into this standalone source corpus.
sources.claim: Tested steady-field arrangements yielded no identified anomalous force; residual torque depended on shielding, and powered-varistor outgassing complicated inference.
sources.limits: Does not establish: a universal exclusion of every gravity-modification model, or sensitivity reproduced by this project. Publisher fetch failed; PMC required a browser challenge. Author PDF was read. Some residuals are upper limits, not exactly zero.
sources.provenance: Tajmar, Kößling and Neunzig; primary experimental preprint linked to Scientific Reports 14, 19427.
sources.version: Author preprint v2; journal DOI 10.1038/s41598-024-70286-w published 2024-08-21

sources.title: Asymmetrical Capacitors for Propulsion
sources.sections: Selected printed pp. 2–4 background, pp. 7–8 experimental observations, pp. 11–16 model/conclusions.
sources.readDepth: Selected full text read earlier in this session; carried into this standalone source corpus.
sources.claim: Their observed air thrust was consistent with ion momentum transferred to gas; grounding changed force direction in some geometries.
sources.limits: Does not establish: nASA confirmation of antigravity or a universal high-vacuum thrust bound. The rotation apparatus had a finite coarse threshold; an isolated arc event is not sustained vacuum thrust.
sources.provenance: Canning, Melcher and Winet; NASA contractor technical report.

sources.title: US11511891B2 System and method for generating forces using asymmetrical electrostatic pressure

sources.readDepth: Selected full text read earlier in this session; carried into this standalone source corpus.
sources.claim: The inventors claim an electrostatic-pressure force and distinguish it from familiar alternatives. The selected record states federally sponsored research is not applicable.
sources.limits: Does not establish: independent replication, NASA validation, gravity modification or proof of a closed-system thrust. Selected claims do not replace raw calibrated whole-apparatus data. Legal status is not assessed.

sources.title: Nonlinear dynamics of diamagnetically levitating resonators
sources.sections: Selected abstract, introduction and §2.1 experimental methods.
sources.readDepth: Selected full text read earlier in this session; carried into this standalone source corpus.
sources.claim: A graphite plate above an alternating magnet array is supported by magnetic force against weight; amplitude-dependent stiffness and damping affect its resonances.
sources.limits: Does not establish: gravity shielding, source-free propulsion or a reproduced low-cost precision resonator. Exact experiment uses laser/vacuum instrumentation; no raw data analyzed here.
sources.provenance: Chen, de Lint, Alijani and Steeneken; primary experimental article.

sources.title: DMRadio-Core: A new approach for GUT-scale axion searches
sources.sections: § II opening/Eq. 1/Fig. 1; § III.1 pickup/slit current path; § IV.1 Fig. 4; advisor additionally inspected Eq. 2.
sources.readDepth: Selected primary design-preprint sections; no raw-data replication.
sources.claim: Authors propose segmented-solenoid/LC-pickup geometry and project sensitivity with numerical modeling.
sources.limits: Proposal is not axion detection. Header v1 date 17 April 2026 differs from body 24 August 2026. Advisor flags Eq. 2 angular/cyclic-frequency notation: do not import without resolving 2π.

sources.title: The search for low-mass axion dark matter with ABRACADABRA-10cm
sources.sections: Main calibration/veto/analysis paragraphs; supplementary§ III Eq. S1 and magnet-on/off flux-noise comparison.
sources.readDepth: Selected primary full-text methods/results; full pipeline not reproduced.
sources.claim: End-to-end flux calibration and environmental/magnet-off vetoes support a bounded search; this 2021 search found no significant axion evidence.
sources.limits: Injected calibration is equivalent only up to geometry; a resonant laboratory peak alone is not an axion. This older search is not a statement about every current result.
sources.provenance: Salemi et al. primary search; PRL 127, 081801.
sources.accessNotes: Generic PDF and erroneous v3 HTML failed; version 1 linked from the abstract was accessible.

sources.title: Noise limits for dc SQUID readout of high-Q resonators below 300 MHz
sources.sections: Abstract; § III matching to resonator, Eqs. 14, 17–21; selected amplifier-chain discussion.
sources.readDepth: Selected primary methods; no cryogenic device replicated.
sources.claim: Readout matching depends on added inductance, imprecision, backaction and their correlations.
sources.limits: Largest output amplitude is not automatically best sensitivity; quantum noise results do not transfer to a toy receiver. Metadata submitted 29 April 2025 but rendered body date 24 August 2026.
sources.provenance: Ankel et al. primary noise/readout study.
